question: Muhammad Ghori attacked Tabarhinda (Bhatinda) in 1191, a strategic point for ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prithviraj Chauhan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1191 Muhammad Ghori attacked and captured Bhatinda, a part of Prithviraj dominion.
 
• This led Muhammad to come into a direct clash with Prithviraj Chauhan one of the most powerful Rajput rulers.
 
• It is known as the First Battle of Tarain.
 
• Muhammad Ghori was defeated in the battle and also wounded in the arm. The Muslim army was routed and the battle was completely won over by the Rajputs.
 
• **Prithviraj Chauhan**__
 __
 
• He was an Indian king from the Chahamana(Chauhan) dynasty.
 
• From the early years, Prithviraj Chauhan showed his sharpness and brilliance by learning all military skills.
 
• It was believed he mastered the skills of aiming the target based on its sound, known as the "Shabhbhedi" technique.
 
• His grandfather Angam, the ruler of Delhi, declared him the heir to the throne of Delhi.
 
• His defeat at Tarain is seen as a landmark event in the Islamic conquest of India and has been described in several semi-legendary accounts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Ghori**__

 
 
• He was the founder of a Muslim ruler in India. He ruled from 1173 to 1206.
 
• He is known to have started the Slave Dynasty and was the first of the Five sultanates which ruled Delhi before the Mughals.
 
• It was the second Battle of Tarain which opened the Delhi area to Muhammad Ghori. In 1192 AD, he invaded again after the 1191 AD invasion with more soldiers and weapons. He defeated Prithvi Raj Chauhan and captured Delhi.
 
• He was a Sunni Muslim who was instrumental in establishing Islamic supremacy in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• In 1206, He was murdered and his kingdom in northern India was left in the control of his general Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
